critical_code_review_comments: Header.jsx line 128: 'dropdown-password' item routes to /profil (same as dropdown-profile) — this is intentional per current spec (profile page contains change-password section), but consider deep-linking to a hash like /profil#change-password so the section is scrolled/highlighted for better UX.

Leaderboard.jsx retains an unused exportXlsx() helper (lines 47-59) — the button is now hidden and export is triggered from Header dropdown. The dead handler can be removed to reduce duplication with Header.jsx downloadXlsx(). Currently harmless but violates DRY.

Both exportXlsx (Leaderboard) and downloadXlsx (Header) trigger XLSX download via anchor <a href=... .click()> — this relies on browser session cookies/JWT. Since JWT is in localStorage as Bearer, the anchor download won't send Authorization header. GET /api/export/xlsx returns 200 in tests only because the endpoint is likely public (verified: response 200 without explicit auth header in my request from browser context which also lacked the Bearer header on the anchor). If auth is later enforced, this download will break — flag for future hardening. Consider using api.get('/export/xlsx', {responseType:'blob'}) instead.
